Follow the awards

SpaceX and Blue Origin secured the largest named awards in this sample, primarily for crew lander development and demonstration. The ledger is neither a spending history nor a profit ranking.

Source ledger

AnnouncementValueSource
How to read the ledger

Amounts are original nominal U.S. dollars reported by NASA unless an incremental modification is identified. The named chart sums only selected named awards, not pooled task orders, options, ceilings, or obligations. An awarded modification (such as SpaceX’s HLS Option B) is not the same as an unexercised option. A ceiling caps potential orders; it is not a commitment, and it must not be added to task orders beneath it.

For comparison, NASA’s OIG previously projected about $93B of Artemis campaign costs across FY2012–2025 ↗. That broader historical projection includes programs outside this ledger and is not a current market size or a company award.

Revenue by service

SHARE OF MODELED SPEND
    Model assumptions and supplier shares

    Annual service revenue = quantity × unit price. Operator revenue = sum of each service’s revenue × that operator’s assumed share. The allocation models pooled, independently purchased services; don’t enter a launch, fuel load, or other pass-through item separately if it is already bundled into a modeled landing or cargo contract. Fractions of a service represent an average allocation, not partial flights.

    All prices, demand, and shares are illustrative inputs, not contract rates or market forecasts. “Other suppliers” is a residual bucket, not a firm. The model does not include costs, margins, China’s state program spending, or all providers. In particular, commercial lunar depot operations and interfaces are not established, and Orbit Fab’s storable fuel work does not validate lunar cryogenic refueling.

    Revenue and operational control are different.

      NASA / PUBLIC DOMAIN
      Sources, readiness labels, and map assumptions

      Research snapshot: 19 November 2026. Each briefing opens its own sources. Dates labeled Target are stated goals, Awarded records procurement rather than delivery, and Scenario is an illustrative possibility, not a forecast. Readiness describes the capability discussed, not an audited numerical Technology Readiness Level (TRL) or whole-company rating. Contract amounts are announced values, not necessarily obligations or cash earned.

      Orbit sizes and distances are not to scale. L1 and L2 are Earth–Moon rotating-frame reference points; NRHO (near-rectilinear halo orbit) is a three-body orbit, not a circular parking orbit. The map’s Hohmann-type path is an idealized direct-transfer analogy, not a two-body solution for lunar capture. The ballistic path illustrates a lower-energy class of routes that often takes longer and can exploit solar perturbations.

      NASA Moon facts ↗ · NASA Lagrange points ↗ · Gateway architecture reference ↗. Hero and engineering artwork are illustrations; the photo cards are credited separately.
